title: Good News for Beef Lovers

image.attribution: J. Samuel Burner / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.0

main_content:
America’s cows are as fat as they’ve ever been, which could lead to lower prices for beef lovers. According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the average weight of a cow sold to beef processors was 630 kilograms in October, an all-time high.

The reason is that feedlot owners, facing a glut of cattle and lower demand for beef by consumers, are keeping the cows longer and allowing them to gorge on cheap feed to gain even more weight.

“It still makes economic sense” to put as much weight on, as efficiently as you can, to minimize losses” feedlot owner Tom Fanning told Bloomberg. He added that despite the extra weight, he still loses $100 to $300 on each animal he sells to slaughterhouses.

Fanning said cows typically spend 150 days at the feedlot before being sold. That is up by 25 days from just two years ago, he said. A cow gains about two kilograms per day, he said.

Cattle futures are down a whopping 22 percent from an all-time high one year ago, reported Farm Journal. A main driver is the increasing supply of steers as ranchers recover from the 2012 drought that thinned the herds.

Wholesale beef prices have plummeted by 23 percent as well, and soon, those prices will likely be reflected at the retail level.

questions.question: What do heavier cows mean for beef consumers?
options: A possible increase in the quality of beef they purchase
A trend that is likely to raise beef prices in the long run
Lower prices for beef products due to an oversupply
A reduced availability of beef in the market
questions.answer: Lower prices for beef products due to an oversupply

questions.question: Why are cows in the U.S. getting heavier?
options: Feedlot owners are rushing cows to market to reduce costs
Ranchers have increased the quality of cattle feed
Lower demand for beef causes cows to be kept longer on feedlots
Economic incentives have led to a decrease in cattle numbers
questions.answer: Lower demand for beef causes cows to be kept longer on feedlots

questions.question: How fast do cows gain in weight?
options: An average of five kilograms per week
